thread:
Maya (marketing): @Riley and @Priya quick sync — SparkBridge interview recording is scheduled for next Wed at 10am PT. We need: final quote approval, signed release, and a short 1-paragraph customer blurb for the launch post.
Riley (producer): Got it. I've booked a 45m Zoom and set up local recording + backup. Will send asset checklist after the interview.
Ethan - CS: Can we tighten the quote to avoid the superlatives? Customer asked earlier for a softer line.
Maya (marketing): Good call. @Ethan do you have suggested language? We want something punchy but factual for the case study.
Ethan - CS: Suggestion: "Using Redwood reduced inference costs by 38% while improving 99th percentile latency for our key workflows." keeps it concrete.
Priya (Legal): That phrasing is fine but we need the customer's approval on the percentage and on any performance claims. Also need signed release that covers use in web, social, and webinar.
Maya (marketing): Understood. @Riley can you add a short consent checkbox in the doc and get them to initial the percentage?
Riley (producer): Yep — I'll include a one-line consent and a place for initials. Drafting now.
calendar-bot: Suggested slots posted: Wed 10:00-10:45 PT, Thu 9:00-9:45 PT, Fri 1:00-1:45 PT — click to add to calendar: https://calendar.example/sparkbridge
Maya (marketing): We prefer Wed 10. @Jon R can you confirm webinar mention approval? We plan to highlight the case study in our June benchmarks webinar.
Jon R: Approved. Please avoid disclosing any client-specific SLAs or customer revenue numbers. Webinar blurb should be product-focused.
Priya (Legal): Also: need NDA/PR release signed. Upload to shared drive and tag me. If customer proposes edits, have them highlight redlines so we can triage quickly.
Maya (marketing): Copy. I'll upload the release and a draft quote.
Riley (producer): Draft release (inline) — feel free to copy/paste and send to customer: 

```
Customer Release Agreement: Customer grants Redwood Inference a non-exclusive right to use Customer name, logo, and a 300-word case study excerpt for marketing purposes including website, social, webinars, and press releases. Customer confirms accuracy of quoted metrics and authorizes Redwood to publish upon signing. Customer may request redlines within 5 business days.
```

Riley (producer): I'll also include a short pre-interview form for the customer with three prompts: 1) Top 3 measurable benefits; 2) One-sentence summary for the web; 3) Any restricted topics.
Maya (marketing): Perfect. Once they sign, can someone run the quote through the benchmark team to validate the 38% figure? Tagging @Ethan for handoff.
Ethan - CS: I’ll pull the telemetry and export the comparison table. Expect that by EOD Tuesday.
Priya (Legal): One more thing — add a data retention line: "Redwood will retain recording and assets for 24 months unless otherwise agreed." Customer needs to acknowledge.
Maya (marketing): Added. Last item: lead routing. After publish, we want inbound demo requests routed to AE inbox + tagging as "sparkbridge-case-study". @Jon R can ops set that up?
Jon R: Yes, I'll add a routing rule in HubSpot: tag + 2-day follow-up task for SDR.
Maya (marketing): Amazing. Plan: send release and pre-interview form today, ask them to sign within 3 business days, record Wed 10, get quote validated by Tuesday EOD, and legal sign-off before publish.
Riley (producer): I'll send calendar invite + Zoom link and a short rundown for the customer.
Priya (Legal): Please CC me on the signed release so I can close the file.
Maya (marketing): Thanks team :rocket: — tracking in the thread.
Jon R: :thumbsup:
Ethan - CS: Thanks — will share the telemetry export in this thread when ready.
Riley (producer): Quick note — if customer requests anonymization we can use initials and blur logo. Flag it asap.
Maya (marketing): Good call. If that happens we'll swap the quote to a non-identifying form and hold publication until legal confirms.
Priya (Legal): Sounds good.
Maya (marketing): End of thread for now — I'll post updates after they return the form.
